content: No tree becomes deep-rooted and sturdy unless frequent gales buffet it.
author: Seneca
story:
This insight touches directly on the messy reality of human nature. Hardship is not an unfair interruption to your real life—it is the very forge in which character is tempered. No one develops deep wisdom, empathy, or stamina by cruising down an easy path without resistance.

In Seneca's view, genuine strength is not an abstract theory—it is a lived, daily practice. Like a tree that develops deeper roots when buffeted by winter gales, your past trials gave you a reservoir of strength you didn't know you possessed. You are more durable than your anxious thoughts give you credit for.
reflectionPrompt: When you look back on past hardships, how did navigating them expand your capacity for strength?
